summary: This program builds a small library of Book objects in an ArrayList, then walks through that list and copies every book whose genre is Fantasy into a second list, which it prints. It shows how to filter a collection without disturbing the original.

lines.text: This is the separate pile you set aside for your friend: a new list that will hold only the matching books, while the original library list stays exactly as it was.
The enhanced for loop hands you each Book in the collection one at a time, so you never have to manage an index or worry about how many books there are.

The filter criterion asks each book for its genre through its getter. Using equalsIgnoreCase rather than == means "fantasy", "Fantasy", and "FANTASY" all match, which is what you want when comparing text.
Only the object reference is added to the second list, so both lists point at the same Book; nothing is copied or removed from the library.
A second loop prints the subset, and passing the Book straight to println works because the Book class defines a toString method that formats its own details.
